government_ids.name: Philippine Identification System (PhilSys National ID)
government_ids.description: An official government-issued identification system containing a unique permanent PhilSys Number (PSN), biometric data (facial image, iris scan, fingerprints), and a QR code for secure digital verification. Available in physical card, paper format (ePhilID), and mobile app (Digital National ID) versions.
government_ids.eligibility: All Filipino citizens (living in the Philippines or abroad) and foreign residents residing in the Philippines for at least six (6) months.
government_ids.requirements:
NEW APPLICATION (FILIPINO CITIZENS):
1. PRIMARY SUPPORTING DOCUMENTS The registrant is encouraged to bring any ONE (1) of the following primary documents (Original Copy):
• PSA-issued Certificate of Live Birth AND one (1) government-issued ID bearing full name, front-facing photo, and signature/thumbmark
• Philippine Passport or ePassport (DFA)
• Unified Multi-purpose Identification (UMID) Card (GSIS or SSS)
• Student Permit, Non-Professional Driver’s License, or Professional Driver’s License (LTO) (Note: In case of discrepancies between the PSA Birth Certificate and the government ID presented, the entry in the PSA Birth Certificate shall prevail).
2. SECONDARY SUPPORTING DOCUMENTS If no primary document is available, the applicant may submit any ONE (1) of the following secondary documents (Original Copy):
• PSA-issued / NSO-issued Certificate of Live Birth with Birth Reference Number (BReN)
• Local Civil Registry Office (LCRO)-issued Certificate of Live Birth
• PSA-issued Report of Birth or Certificate of Foundling
• Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP) ID
• Professional Regulatory Commission (PRC) ID
• Seaman’s Book (Seafarer’s Record Book) or Seafarer’s Identity Document (Seaman’s ID)
• Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA) ID
• Senior Citizen’s ID (OSCA / LGU)
• Social Security System (SSS) ID
• Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps) ID
• License to Own or Possess Firearms (LTOPF)
• National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Clearance
• Police Clearance / Police ID
• Solo Parent’s ID
• Person with Disability (PWD) ID (NCDA, Mayor's Office, DSWD, or DOH-partnered organizations)
• Voter’s ID (COMELEC)
• Postal ID (PHLPost)
• Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) Card
• PhilHealth ID
• Special Resident Retiree’s Visa (SRRV)
• National ID or Residence ID from other countries
• Professional Identification Card (MARINA)
• Civil Service Commission (CSC) Eligibility Card
• Dependent’s ID (AFP / PNP)
• Retiree’s ID (PNP, AFP, PCG)
• Conductor’s License (LTO)
• Philippine Veterans Affairs Office (PVAO) Pensioner’s ID
• Tribal Certificate/ID (Tribal Affairs Office) or Certificate of Confirmation/Membership (NCIP / ICC / IP / NCMF)
3. ADDITIONAL SECONDARY DOCUMENTS (Requires photo, signature/thumbmark, full name, permanent address, and birthdate):
• Employee ID
• School ID (for pre-school, elementary, and high school; signature/thumbmark of ID owner is not required)
• City / Municipal ID
• Barangay Clearance / Barangay Certificate / Barangay ID
• Voter’s Certification (COMELEC)
• Prison Record or Certificate of Detention
government_ids.processing_time: Digital and paper-format availability and physical-card delivery vary. Check with PSA; no guaranteed instant generation or delivery deadline is encoded.
government_ids.validity: Confirm applicant-specific validity and biometric updating rules with PSA. The supplied lifetime/one-year claims are retained in the source archive pending targeted review.
government_ids.purpose: Serves as a single, foundational government-issued proof of identity to simplify public and private transactions, promote financial inclusion, and streamline access to social protection services.
government_ids.eligibility_other_conditions: All Filipino citizens (living in the Philippines or abroad) and foreign residents residing in the Philippines for at least six (6) months.
government_ids.prerequisite_notes: PSA Birth Certificate or any accepted primary/secondary supporting document.
government_ids.application_process:
(NEW APPLICATION - WALK-IN):
1. Visit Registration Center: Proceed to any operational PhilSys Registration Center (Fixed PSA offices, municipal halls, or mall-based booths). No online pre-registration or appointment is needed.
2. Document Screening: Present your original primary or secondary supporting documents to the Registration Kit Operator.
3. Biometric Capture: Have your demographic data validated and biometrics captured (front-facing photograph, 10-fingerprint scan, dual-iris scan).
4. Review Information: Carefully review and confirm your encoded demographic details on the display screen.
5. Collect Transaction Slip: Receive your official transaction slip containing your unique Transaction Reference Number (TRN). DIGITAL NATIONAL ID GENERATION (ONLINE STEP-BY-STEP):
1. Download the eGovPH Mobile App or visit https://philsys.gov.ph/
2. Create an account using your active mobile number and select Digital National ID .
3. Enter your Transaction Reference Number (TRN) from your registration slip.
4. Complete the mandatory live facial recognition check on your smartphone.
5. Access, view, or screenshot your official Digital National ID for immediate use in transactions.
government_ids.renewal_process: Not applicable for adult Filipino citizens (lifetime validity). Mandatory biometric recapture and renewal are required for foreign residents (annually) and minors upon reaching age 5 and age 18.
government_ids.replacement_process:
(UPDATE DETAILS / LOST CARD):
• Updating Demographic Data: Visit a registration center with supporting documents (e.g., Marriage Certificate or corrected Birth Certificate) for validation.
• Lost / Stolen Card: Present a notarized Affidavit of Loss (or police blotter for stolen cards), a primary/secondary ID, pay a replacement fee (₱200–₱400), and undergo biometric verification.
• Damaged Card: Surrender physical damaged card at a registration center alongside valid supporting ID and undergo biometric verification (₱135–₱400; free if due to manufacturing defect).

government_ids.name: Philippine Passport (ePassport)
government_ids.description: An official government-issued travel document and primary ID for Filipino citizens. It contains your photo, personal details, and secure digital data used for identity verification and international travel.
government_ids.purpose: An official identification card and travel document used to certify the identity and Philippine citizenship of the holder for international travel, identity verification, and general transaction purposes across public and private sectors.

government_ids.name: Postal ID
government_ids.description: A functional government ID issued by PHLPost. It contains security features and biometrics and is accepted for various government and private transactions.
government_ids.purpose: An identification card used to verify the identity and address of an individual. It is one of the most accessible government IDs and is used for mail delivery verification and general identification.

government_ids.name: Unified Multi-Purpose ID (UMID) — legacy
government_ids.description: The UMID card contains the cardholder’s personal information such as name, address and date of birth as well as a front-facing photograph and signature. It also includes the unique Common Reference Number (CRN) which doubles as the ID number. The card comes with security features embedded such as a magnetic strip and a contactless chip that stores the personal data of the cardholder.
government_ids.purpose: The Unified Multi-Purpose ID (UMID) is a single card used for transactions with various government agencies, including SSS, GSIS, PhilHealth, and Pag-IBIG. It integrates multiple social security services into one platform.

government_ids.name: MySSS Card
government_ids.description: The MySSS Card is an official SSS functional ID equipped with an advanced EMV chip and integrated with the National ID (PhilSys) eVerify system. It serves as a secure physical card carrying the member's biometric data, replacing older formats like the legacy SSS ID and UMID.
government_ids.purpose: Its primary purpose is dual-fold: it acts as an identity verification card for SSS-related transactions, and it functions as a linked bank debit card that automatically receives loan proceeds, sickness/maternity benefits, and monthly pensions without requiring separate disbursement account setups.

government_ids.name: GSIS Digital ID
government_ids.description: An app-based digital credential generated inside the GSIS Touch mobile application. It replaces the legacy physical UMID/eCard and displays the member's profile, BP Number, and digital QR verification. (Note: Physical UMID card issuance was officially phased out on May 31, 2024.)
government_ids.purpose: Serves as the primary virtual identification document for active government employees and pensioners to access GSIS services, verify membership records, and execute online transactions.

government_ids.name: PRC (Professional Identification Card)
government_ids.description: The PRC ID contains important information such as the professional’s name, photograph, profession, registration number, date of registration, validity/expiration date, and signature . It is commonly presented when applying for jobs, verifying professional credentials, renewing a professional license, and performing transactions that require proof of professional registration.
government_ids.purpose: The PRC ID (Professional Identification Card) serves as the official identification and proof of registration of a professional who is licensed by the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) . It shows that the holder is legally authorized to practice their profession in the Philippines.

government_ids.name: Student Driver's Permit (Student Permit)
government_ids.description: An official permit document or card issued by the Land Transportation Office confirming that the holder has completed theoretical driving requirements and is legally permitted to practice driving under proper supervision.
government_ids.purpose: Serves as the initial official authorization issued by the LTO allowing a student driver to operate a motor vehicle on public highways while undergoing practical driving instruction under the supervision of a licensed driver.
government_ids.official_sources:
Source PDF pages 26–28. Supplied research; no verification date assigned.

Original sources: Land Transportation Office (LTO) / LTO NCR Portal
• Republic Act No. 10930 and related LTO Memorandum Circulars (including MC 2020-2194)

Full supplied validity: Valid for one (1) year from the date of issuance. After one (1) year, it cannot be used for the practical driving course, though it can still be used to apply for a Non-Professional Driver's License if the practical driving course was completed within the one-year validity. After two (2) years from issuance, holders must acquire a new student permit bearing the same number and undergo the required apprenticeship period.

government_ids.name: Non-Professional Driver's License (NPDL)
government_ids.description: An official card-based driver's license issued to motorists who have passed both the theoretical and practical driving examinations and completed all prerequisite student driver requirements.
government_ids.purpose: Serves as the official legal authorization issued by the LTO enabling a qualified individual to drive private motor vehicles on public roads.
government_ids.official_sources:
Source PDF pages 29–30. Supplied research; no verification date assigned.

Original sources: Land Transportation Office (LTO) / LTO NCR Portal

government_ids.name: Professional Driver's License (PDL)
government_ids.description: An official card-based driver's license issued to motorists who meet the age, legal clearance, and driving experience prerequisites, and have successfully passed advanced theoretical and practical examinations for professional restriction codes.
government_ids.purpose: Serves as the official legal authorization issued by the LTO enabling a qualified individual to drive or operate commercial, public utility, or private motor vehicles for hire or a living.
government_ids.official_sources:
Source PDF pages 31–32. Supplied research; no verification date assigned.

Original sources: Land Transportation Office (LTO) Philippines

government_ids.name: Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN)
government_ids.description: A unique identifying number supplied or assigned to taxpayers to be indicated in all returns, statements, or documents filed with the BIR.
government_ids.purpose: Serves as a proper identification for tax purposes, required under the authority of the Internal Revenue Code for any person, whether natural or juridical, to make, render, or file a return, statement, or other documents with the BIR.
government_ids.official_sources:
Source PDF pages 33–34. Supplied research; no verification date assigned.

Original sources: Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) National Internal Revenue Code (NIRC) and Revenue Regulations (RR No. 7-2012, RR No. 7-2024).

Full supplied fee: Loose DST: Payment of P30.00 loose Documentary Stamp Tax (DST) to be affixed on the Certificate of Registration (COR) for business/corporate registrations (or free/none if processed online without loose DST requirements, or for pure employee/EO 98 registrations which have no fees).
• Printing Cost: Procured printing cost of BIR Printed Invoices (BPI), if opted to use.

government_ids.name: OWWA OFW eCard (Overseas Workers Welfare Administration eCard)
government_ids.description: A digital and physical identification card issued to registered Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) with active OWWA membership, containing a unique permanent membership tracking number.
government_ids.purpose: Serves as official proof of active OWWA membership and functions as a valid government-issued identification card for official transactions in the Philippines and abroad, providing quick access to OWWA programs, services, and partner benefits.
government_ids.official_sources:
Source PDF pages 35–36. Supplied research; no verification date assigned.

Original sources: Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA) / Department of Migrant Workers (DMW)

government_ids.name: Office of the Senior Citizen Affairs (OSCA) ID
government_ids.description: An official laminated ID card issued to qualified elderly citizens containing a unique control number, personal photo, and signature.
government_ids.purpose: Provides official identification enabling senior citizens to avail of statutory 20% discounts and VAT exemptions on medicines, medical services, transport, public utilities, restaurants, and recreation, plus priority queuing privileges.
government_ids.official_sources:
Source PDF pages 42–44. Supplied research; no verification date assigned.

Original sources: Republic Act No. 7432 (Senior Citizens Act) as amended by RA 9994.

government_ids.name: Persons with Disability (PWD) ID
government_ids.description: An official card bearing a unique PWD registration number, type of disability, photograph, and signature of the municipal mayor/PDAO head.
government_ids.purpose: Grants qualified individuals statutory privileges, discounts, and exemptions on medical costs, transport fares, public utilities, and priority government services under Magna Carta mandates.

government_ids.name: Solo Parent Identification Card
government_ids.description: An official municipal card certifying solo parent status, featuring a unique control number and identifying details.
government_ids.purpose: Entitles qualified single parents to parental leave, educational scholarships, medical subsidies, housing assistance, and priority assistance under the Solo Parents' Welfare Act.
government_ids.official_sources:
Source PDF pages 42–44. Supplied research; no verification date assigned.

Original sources: Republic Act No. 8972 (Solo Parents' Welfare Act) as amended by RA 11861.

documents.name: Community Tax Certificate (Cedula)
documents.issued_by: Municipal Treasurer’s Office / authorized barangay treasurer
documents.description: A certificate issued upon payment of community tax. It records the taxpayer’s identifying information and payment for the stated year.

documents.name: Barangay First-Time Jobseeker Certification
documents.description: A barangay certification confirming residency and first-time jobseeker status, used when requesting covered employment documents under the First Time Jobseekers Assistance Act.

documents.name: Barangay Business Clearance
documents.issued_by: Barangay government where the business is located
documents.description: A barangay clearance for a business operating within its jurisdiction, used in business permit applications.

documents.name: Barangay Clearance
documents.description: A clearance issued by the barangay based on its records, commonly requested for employment and other transactions.

documents.name: Certificate of Residency
documents.description: A certification confirming that a person resides at an address within the barangay.

documents.name: Certificate of Indigency
documents.description: A barangay certification of a resident’s financial circumstances, commonly used to support requests for assistance.

documents.name: Certificate of Good Moral Character
documents.description: A barangay certification concerning a resident’s character and conduct within the community.

documents.name: Barangay Blotter Report
documents.description: A record of an incident or complaint reported to the barangay. A copy documents the report made; it is not a court decision.

documents.name: Local Birth Certificate Copy
documents.issued_by: Local Civil Registrar where the birth was registered
documents.description: A certified copy of a birth record kept by the Local Civil Registrar, containing the registered details of the birth and parentage.

documents.name: Local Marriage Certificate Copy
documents.issued_by: Local Civil Registrar where the marriage was registered
documents.description: A certified copy of a marriage record kept by the Local Civil Registrar, containing the registered details of the spouses and marriage.

documents.name: Local Death Certificate Copy
documents.issued_by: Local Civil Registrar where the death was registered
documents.description: A certified copy of a death record kept by the Local Civil Registrar, containing the registered details of the deceased and death.

documents.name: Marriage License
documents.description: A license issued before a marriage is solemnized in cases where a marriage license is required.

documents.name: Real Property Tax Clearance
documents.description: A certification of the real property tax payment status of a specified property for the period covered.

documents.name: Tax Declaration
documents.description: A property assessment record describing real property and its assessed value for taxation purposes. It is distinct from a land title.

documents.name: National Police Clearance
documents.description: A clearance issued through the PNP National Police Clearance System following an identity and records check.

documents.name: NBI Clearance
documents.description: A clearance issued by the National Bureau of Investigation following an identity and records check, commonly requested for employment and other transactions.

documents.name: PSA Birth Certificate
documents.description: A PSA-issued copy of a registered birth record, used to establish birth details and parentage.

documents.name: PSA Marriage Certificate
documents.description: A PSA-issued copy of a registered marriage record, used as documentary evidence of the marriage.

documents.name: PSA Death Certificate
documents.description: A PSA-issued copy of a registered death record, used to document a person’s death.

documents.name: PSA CENOMAR
documents.description: A Certificate of No Marriage Record issued by PSA, certifying that no marriage record was found for the person in its records.

documents.name: Income Tax Return / BIR Tax Filing
documents.issued_by: Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) — filed by the taxpayer
documents.description: A tax return filed with BIR declaring income and the applicable income tax information for a reporting period. The form used depends on the taxpayer and filing type.

documents.name: Voter's Certification
documents.description: A certification issued by COMELEC concerning a person’s voter registration record.

If details differ between your PSA birth certificate and the government ID presented, PSA states that the birth-certificate entries prevail.
The operator validates your demographic details and captures applicable biometrics, including a front-facing photograph, fingerprints, and iris scans.
Biometric capture depends on age and applicable PSA rules. Ask the operator about children or applicants unable to provide a biometric.
Carefully review your encoded demographic and biometric information before confirming it.
Report spelling errors or incorrect details to the operator before completing registration.
Collect the transaction slip containing your Transaction Reference Number (TRN).
Keep the slip for delivery tracking and checking availability of the National ID in paper format. Ask PSA about current delivery or claiming arrangements.
Use https://national-id.gov.ph/ or the eGovPH mobile app.
This is for people already registered in the National ID system. It is not a new registration.
Follow the official service prompts and enter your demographic information as registered with PSA.
Your TRN is not seeded as a mandatory digital-access credential; PSA’s published digital-access guidance specifies demographic information and facial verification.
Follow the live facial-verification prompts to confirm your identity.
After successful verification and when your record is available, view or obtain your Digital National ID through the official service.
Availability is not guaranteed immediately after registration. Contact PSA if the service cannot find or verify your record.
Documents to prepare

content.body: PSA’s updating service is free of charge. Confirm the accepted proof for your requested change.
Present your National ID and supporting documents at a selected registration center offering updating services.
Do not register a second time to change your information. Confirm the center offers updating before visiting.
For a lost, stolen, or damaged card, contact PSA or a registration center to confirm current replacement availability and required documents.
The supplied ₱200–₱400 and ₱135–₱400 ranges were not verified against an official fee schedule and are not encoded as payable fees.
Bring the proof and supporting documents requested by PSA; retain a damaged card if applicable.
Ask about any applicable fee or exemption before paying. Do not register again simply because the card was lost or damaged.
